p: The video demonstrates reviewing an AI-generated spec doc using Artifact Share. A user highlights text, comments asking for a 3-week version, runs a CLI command to apply comments with Claude, and shows the updated document live at the same URL with resolved comments.
Artifact Share lets teams review and comment directly on AI-generated docs, allowing coding agents to automatically apply revisions to the same URL.

[{"timestamp":"00:00.000","observation":"Hook text overlay poses the question of who reviews agent-written specs."},{"timestamp":"00:05.000","observation":"Text in the shared document is highlighted and a comment is added asking for a 3-week cut."},{"timestamp":"00:12.000","observation":"Terminal CLI shows Claude running 'apply the review comments' and republishing."},{"timestamp":"00:23.400","observation":"Final CTA end card displays product link and core proposition."}]

The workflow is clear and demonstrates the core value proposition directly. Pacing is steady, although transitions between document UI and terminal feel slightly abrupt. Overall, it serves the target audience well with clean typography and legible UI elements.

p: ["CTA button text ('Try it free → artifactshare.com') is low-contrast white-on-light-blue, nearly unreadable at speed","on-screen hook copy ('You comment. Right on the doc.') doesn't match the briefed hook ('Your agent wrote the spec. Who reviews it?'), so the opening lacks the intended provocative question","pacing relies on static doc screenshots with little motion, weakening scroll-stop power despite legible product framing"]

The product loop (share doc → human comments → agent edits via CLI → republish → CTA) is told cleanly and the Artifact Share badge/URL stays visible in every frame, giving strong salience and clarity for a dev audience. The terminal frame with 'claude -p / Codex / Cursor / any agent with a CLI' is the strongest beat and lands the 'any agent' message well. Weakest link is the end card: the primary CTA button text is washed out against its background, undermining click intent right when it matters most, and the opening frame doesn't deliver the sharper 'who reviews the agent's spec' hook from the brief.
